learning_outcomes.text: Identify and describe basic principles and methods in chemistry.
Explain and interpret theoretical and experimental results in chemistry.
Explain fundamental aspects of chemistry: atom and molecules, chemical bonds, substances, laws of chemistry.
Explain and compare mixtures of substances (solutions); define solution concentrations.
Describe water properties and explain water depollution methods.
Define principles of thermodynamics and laws of thermochemistry; describe chemical fuels.
Describe physical and chemical equilibria, explain factors influencing these equilibria.
Define reaction rate and explain factors influencing it.
Explain and compare electrical conduction in metals and electrolyte solutions.
Define terms such as electrolyte, acid, base, salt, oxide.
Define and compare galvanic cells and electrolysis cells.
Define metal corrosion and explain anticorrosion protection methods.
Define lubricants and describe types of lubricants.
Describe main macromolecular compounds with technical applications.
Compare qualitative and quantitative laboratory analyses/methods.
Use stoichiometric calculations for quantitative evaluation.

Apply evaluation criteria and methods for identifying, modeling, experimenting, analyzing, and qualitatively and quantitatively assessing chemical phenomena and processes, including using digital technologies.
Critically evaluate chemical processes, equipment, procedures using specific evaluation instruments and methods.
Operate with basic concepts, principles, and methods in chemistry.
Develop the ability to solve chemistry exercises and problems with applicability in engineering and validate the obtained solution.
Describe physico-chemical phenomena and processes.
Utilize laboratory equipment and digital instruments for chemistry work.
Acquire and process data, interpret theoretical and experimental results.

Respect ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.
Integrate into the work group and apply relationship and efficient work techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
Continuously inform and document themselves in their field of activity by appropriately using effective lifelong learning methods and techniques.
Develop professional projects in the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introductory notions: The atom: structure; elementary particles; electronic configuration.
Chemical elements. Periodic table of elements.
Chemical bonds: ionic bond, covalent bond, metallic bond.
Notions of stoichiometric calculation. Laws of chemistry.
Substances and mixtures of substances: Pure substances (classifications, nomenclatures).
Mixtures of substances: molecular solutions (classifications; solution concentration); colloidal systems (classifications; dispersion colloids, association colloids; surfactants).
Natural water, industrial water, and wastewater: Chemical composition, hardness, water treatment methods (softening, demineralization, degassing, etc.).
Pollution and environmental protection.
Chemical Thermodynamics. Thermochemistry: Principles of thermodynamics (0, I and II principles). Internal Energy, Enthalpy, Entropy, Thermodynamic Potentials.
Thermochemistry. Laws of thermochemistry (Lavoisier-Laplace, Hess, Kirchhoff).
Thermodynamic equilibria: Physical equilibria. Phase diagrams.
Chemical equilibria. Law of chemical equilibrium (law of mass action). Displacement of chemical equilibrium (Le Châtelier - Braun principle). Study of homogeneous and heterogeneous equilibria.
Chemical kinetics: Reaction rate. Factors influencing reaction rate.
Activation of molecules in chemical reactions.
Chain reactions. Combustion, explosions, and thermal flames. Detonation phenomenon.
Electrochemistry: Electrolytes. Electrical conduction in electrolyte solutions.
Electrode processes. Galvanic cells. Electrolysis cells. Electrochemical conversion.
Corrosion and anticorrosion protection of metals: Thermodynamics and kinetics of chemical corrosion; oxidation of metals in dry atmosphere; corrosion in liquid fuels and lubricating oils.

Thermodynamics and kinetics of electrochemical corrosion; passivation phenomena. Electrochemical anticorrosion protection methods (galvanizing, nickel plating, etc.) and thermochemical methods (browning, phosphatization, etc.).
Lubricants: Lubrication (greasing) - Theories of lubrication.
Mineral and synthetic lubricating oils: composition, production, physico-chemical and operational characteristics (viscosity, oiliness, flash point, freezing point, acid number).
Greases: composition, production, physico-chemical and operational characteristics.
Solid and gaseous lubricants.
Fuels: Classification, characteristics, chemical composition. Calorific value.
Combustion processes and calculation of fuel combustion.
Gasoline and diesel. Octane number of gasoline and Diesel index of diesel.
Unconventional fuels for engines.
Macromolecular compounds with technical applications: Plastics, rubbers, polymeric composites. Structural characterization, chemical, mechanical, thermal, electrical properties.
General norms of labor protection and fire safety in practical laboratory activity. General laboratory operations. Stoichiometric calculations.
Solutions: preparation and determination of solution concentration.
Water: determination of water hardness, water softening.
Electrochemistry: electrode potential, galvanic cells.
Metal corrosion: determination of corrosion rate in acidic solution.
Protection of metals against corrosion: galvanic method - galvanizing.
Lubricants: Lubricating oils - determination of viscosity, acid number, and flash point. Greases - determination of dropping point. Final evaluation.
teaching_methods: Short recap of previous course notions
Direct and indirect exploration of reality (experiment, demonstration, modeling)
assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must demonstrate knowledge of basic notions of Chemistry (from the studied chapters), complete all laboratory works, achieve a minimum grade of 5 in the laboratory, and a minimum grade of 5 in the exam. The final evaluation result is determined by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Grades will be awarded on a scale of 1 to 10, with a minimum grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes and associated study credits.
